Low dawn sun raking straight along the cut face so every course throws its own thin shadow, the air cold blue, one hurricane lamp still burning warm on a peg in the trench.
Hard high noon dropping straight down into the trench so the swept floor tiles glare white and the banded face above stands in deep shadow, one warm fire glow outside the canvas.
Late golden afternoon low and warm across the turf so the top two courses go gold and the floor below stays cool blue, one ochre band blazing where the sun catches it.
Sunset with the whole turf lip rimmed hot orange and the trench below gone deep violet, the ochre band catching the last of it and a small fire warm beyond the tent.
Blue hour with the sky deep indigo pressing down into the trench and every band reading dark and saturated, the only warm light a glow inside the canvas.
Full night worked by lamplight, a single hurricane lamp on a peg throwing warm amber light across the banded face while the rest of the field stays black and the sky deep.
Overcast soft even light with every band reading at full chroma against a flat pearl-grey sky, one warm canvas glow the only accent in the cool field.
A storm sky of dark slate overhead and one break of low sun picking the ochre band out in blazing saturated colour against the shadow-dark courses above and below.
After rain, clean washed light falling evenly from every side, the floor plates wet and mirror-bright and every band reading saturated and dark, one warm glow inside the canvas.
Low mist burning off with the sun coming warm and level through it over the lip, the top courses edged gold and the deep floor still cool in blue shadow.
Hard clear high-altitude light under a deep cobalt sky, razor shadows falling straight down the face from every course lip, the floor in full glare and one warm lamp still burning.
Thin winter sun low and pale from the south, long blue shadows lying across white crusted turf and the cut face pale gold on its upper edge, one lamp warm below.
Dust hanging over the lip turned warm ochre by a low sun behind it, the cut face below in cool blue shade and the top course edged bright gold.
Backlit into a low sun so the turf lip reads as a dark frieze and the dust rising above it glows warm, the face below in deep saturated blue shadow.
Frost morning with pale rose light on the top course and deep blue filling the bottom of the trench, the bands reading sharp between them and one warm lamp on a peg.
Midday under thin cloud with soft even light pressing down equally on every course so all bands read full chroma, one lamp left burning warm in the deep shadowed end.
Early morning sun just clearing the eastern lip so it rakes across the face almost horizontally and every course casts a long thin shadow downward, the air still cold and blue.
High summer noon with the sun directly overhead dropping a hard bright disc onto the floor tiles and the entire face in dense shadow, one canvas edge lit warm from inside.
Dusk with the sky going deep amber at the horizon and cool violet directly overhead, the top course washed in orange and the trench floor already dark, a lamp peg glowing.
Late afternoon cross-light coming from low in the west along the length of the trench so one wall is gold and the opposite face stays in blue shade, the air warm.
Pre-dawn with the sky above the lip a saturated deep teal and the trench interior fully dark except for one hurricane lamp on a peg casting warm light across the nearest courses.
Bright midwinter noon with the sun staying low and raking across the face so every course throws a long cold shadow and the floor stays pale, one lamp adding warm amber.
Storm clearing at dusk so the sky is dark slate behind and the low gap in the west lighting the top courses gold while the lip glows.
Dawn with the first direct light just striking the top course in warm pink while the rest of the face remains in cold blue pre-light and the floor is still dark.
Late morning light from a low southeast sun falling across the cut face so the courses on the right go bright and those on the left stay cool, one lamp warm below.
